concepts.def: A community of organisms together with their physical environment.
Shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
Makes its own food by photosynthesis; the start of a food chain.
Breaks down dead matter, recycling nutrients.
Interlinked food chains showing feeding relationships.
Recycles carbon via respiration, photosynthesis, combustion and decay.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecological Relationships — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecological Relationships brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecological Relationships.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a prokaryote?
options: Human skin cell
Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Respiration means breathing — inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.
A series of chemical reactions in cells that break down glucose to release energy as ATP.

mcqs.q: What does the 'all-or-nothing' principle mean for action potentials?
options: Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
Stronger stimuli produce larger action potentials.
Action potentials get bigger as they travel along the axon.
Once threshold is reached, the action potential fires at full size — sub-threshold stimuli produce no action potential.

mcqs.q: How does sweating help cool you down?
options: Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
Sweat is cold and directly cools the skin on contact.
Evaporation of sweat absorbs energy (latent heat) from the skin, lowering body temperature.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell”?
options: Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prokaryotic cell”?
options: Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eukaryotic cell”?
options: Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Subcellular structures”?
options: A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stem cell”?
options: Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Specialised cells”?
options: A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
